newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 2.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 2.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
FRANKFURT - Young children are watching more and more television. A study by Suedwestfunk showed that 3 to 5 year olds spend nearly 90 minutes a day in front of the TV. (Der Spiegel)

BERLIN - Potential investors have declared an interest in taking over Berlin private station Puls TV, which this week declared bankruptcy. Negotiation will continue in the coming weeks, during which time the station says it has sufficient funds to continue 24-hour-a-day broadcasting. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

FRANKFURT - German-Swiss retail group Metro Holding AG plans to offer a telephone and fax service over the Internet in cooperation with Austalia's OzEmail Ltd, a German newspaper reports. The Welt am Sonntag newspaper, in a statement ahead of publication, says the service will start within the year and offer long-distance rates up to 80 percent cheaper than German telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG. (Reuter)

WALLDORF - State premiers Kurt Beck and Erwin Teufel sign an agreement sealing the fusion of their two states' radio and TV stations into Suedwestrundfunk (SWR). The two say SWR will have a yearly broadcasting fee income of around 1.6 billion marks ($94 million), making it the second largest station in the ARD public network. The state parliaments still have to grant their approval. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MUNICH - Troubled German electronics group Grundig will seek to break even in 1998, a year earlier than planned, the group's top executive tells a German magazine in an interview. Grundig management board chairman Pieter de Jong tells the magazine Focus that he believes the group, which was abandoned this year by its backer Philips N.V. due to massive losses, would not survive if it posted losses over the next two years. (Reuter)

MUNICH - News magazine Focus reports Deutsche Telekom plans to buy minority shares in U.S. telecommunications company Sprint with France Telekom. The three companies are currently working together in the Global One alliance. The price is estimated to be about 15 billion marks. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Europe's Airbus plane-making consortium decides to put on hold its restructuring plans to become a single integrated company, a German newspaper reports. Germany's Welt am Sonntag, in a statement released ahead of publication, says the Airbus supervisory board had decided at a May 27 meeting in Toulouse, France, on the change in strategy, which was first announced last January. (Reuter)

VIENNA - The privatisation of Bank Austria looks in peril after a media report says Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank owns the option to buy the 49-percent voting stake held by Vienna City in Austria's number one bank. The city's ruling coalition agreed last Tuesday to relinquish its stake in Bank Austria on the condition that the bank remained under Austrian control. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - A top executive at Allianz AG Holding says in a magazine interview that the German insurance group has not yet ruled out establishing a fund to compensate victims of the Nazis. Allianz management board member Herbert Hansmeyer tells Germany's Der Spiegel magazine that Allianz was contemplating a fund similar to that established by Swiss banks even though he said the insurer lost most of its capital after World War Two. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Jens Volker Schmidtke, chief executive of Internet agency Enternet in Guetersloh, has left for Hamburg agency Contor Interaktiv, where he will serve as project manager.(Kress)

WALLDORF - Ursula Nachtsheim will leave her post as director of the advertising department at convenience products manufacturer Maggi in Frankfurt. Gerald Spitzer, last with Munich MGM, will take over her position. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Kirsten Leung will lead the press department of Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa)'s space infrastructure unit in Bremen, effective June 1. (Kress)
